- When sentiment is negative or trending down, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overreacts and overshoots; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is positive and prices are trending upward, model frequently underestimates the continuation; add 3–7% to forecast mean to capture momentum.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns positive after a downtrend; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods to avoid premature reversal.
- In low-sentiment or flat sentiment periods, model tends to forecast mean-reversion too aggressively; reduce forecast volatility and anchor closer to recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price action (last 5–7 days); increase forecast tail end by 2–5% to reflect potential late rally or volatility accumulation.
